newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent slips, API neutral, but upside seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent slips, API neutral, but upside seen.

text.p: June Brent crude futures slipped in late afternoon dealings on Wednesday in a mild correction to overnight gains after API data was viewed neutral.
June Brent was last traded on SIMEX at $18.60 per barrel, down one cent from London. July was traded at $18.66, down one cent.

Brokers said the American Petroleum Institute data released in the U.S. late on Tuesday was neutral for the market, which had prompted some intraday profit-taking after Tuesday's rises in both London and New York.
However, one broker said the market could be preparing for a short term move higher.
June Brent punctured a June chart gap between $18.64 to $18.77 on Tuesday, but broke through trend line resistance at the same time.
"That's a signal we could be heading higher," he said.
NYMEX June was slightly lower on ACCESS, last trading at $20.36, down eight cents from New York.
